RegAsm.exe (hollowed) beaconing to AsyncRAT C2 / ScreenConnect infra contacts campaign IPs AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the C2 stage: RegAsm.exe — a .NET utility that should never make external network connections — reaching out to the AsyncRAT C2 domain mora1987[.]work[.]gd after process hollowing, plus ScreenConnect/loader processes contacting the campaign's fixed C2 IPs (162.216.241[.]242, 198.23.185[.]81, 2.59.134[.]97) and domains (r.servermanagemen[.]xyz). Article-specific via the concrete C2 indicators and the anomalous RegAsm egress. Rationale: mora1987[.]work[.]gd, r.servermanagemen[.]xyz and the three C2 IPs are article IOCs corroborated by Kaspersky's infrastructure clustering; RegAsm.exe making any public connection is inherently anomalous (it never networks legitimately) and is the AsyncRAT process-hollowing container from the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.esentire.com/blog/exploring-the-infection-chain-screenconnects-link-to-asyncrat-deployment • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/26/poisoned-search-results-gpu-mining-cryptojacking-campaign-abusing-screenconnect-microsoft-net-utilities/
ATT&CKT1055.012 T1071.001 T1219
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A rare .NET dev/build scenario where RegAsm.exe is scripted to reach a package feed (uncommon; verify path and parent)
  • Shared C2 IP later reassigned to a benign hoster (validate against current threat-intel)
  • Proxy/NAT egress attributing the connection to an unexpected source host
  • Internal vuln scanner probing the campaign IPs during authorized testing
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "RegAsm.exe" and RemoteUrl has_any ("nuget.org","microsoft.com") and RemoteIP !in (c2ip))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm RegAsm.exe was spawned suspended by the loader chain (parent = script/cap.ps1 lineage) and correlate the C2 destination against threat-intel; RegAsm networking is by itself high-confidence malicious. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate host, kill RegAsm.exe, block the C2 IPs/domains at perimeter, and remove the ScreenConnect service + persistence task. 3) HUNT: Sweep DeviceNetworkEvents fleet-wide for the C2 IPs/domains and for any RegAsm.exe/AppLaunch.exe public egress; correlate to hosts with the C:\Users\Public loader set.
let c2ip = dynamic(["162.216.241.242","198.23.185.81","2.59.134.97"]);
let c2dom = dynamic(["mora1987.work.gd","r.servermanagemen.xyz"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (c2ip)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (c2dom)
   or (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "RegAsm.exe" and RemoteIPType == "Public")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2ip = dynamic(["162.216.241.242","198.23.185.81","2.59.134.97"]);
let c2dom = dynamic(["mora1987.work.gd","r.servermanagemen.xyz"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (c2ip) or DstHostname has_any (c2dom) or Url has_any (c2dom)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: RegAsm.exe Outbound Network Connection to AsyncRAT/ScreenConnect C2
id: 5c9e2b47-7f31-4a08-b6d2-9a1c4e0f7d68
description: Detects RegAsm.exe (a .NET utility that should not make network connections) initiating an outbound connection, or any host contacting the ScreenConnect/AsyncRAT campaign C2 domains, indicating process hollowing and C2.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/tr/the-soc-files-screenconnect-campaign-with-asyncrat/120472/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/01
tags:
  - attack.t1055.012
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_regasm:
    Image|endswith: '\RegAsm.exe'
    Initiated: 'true'
  selection_c2:
    DestinationHostname:
      - 'mora1987.work.gd'
      - 'r.servermanagemen.xyz'
  condition: selection_regasm or selection_c2
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@DestinationHostname:(mora1987.work.gd OR r.servermanagemen.xyz) OR CIDR(@DestinationIp, 162.216.241.242/32, 198.23.185.81/32, 2.59.134.97/32) OR @Image:(*\RegAsm.exe OR *\regasm.exe OR *\REGASM.EXE))
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 | regex("\\\\RegAsm\.exe$", field=ContextImageFileName) OR RemoteAddressIP4=/^(162\.216\.241\.242|198\.23\.185\.81|2\.59\.134\.97)$/ | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("162.216.241.242","198.23.185.81","2.59.134.97") OR All_Traffic.dest="mora1987.work.gd" OR All_Traffic.dest="r.servermanagemen.xyz") OR (All_Traffic.app="regasm.exe" AND All_Traffic.dest_is_internal="false") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("162.216.241.242","198.23.185.81","2.59.134.97") OR All_Traffic.dest="mora1987.work.gd" OR All_Traffic.dest="r.servermanagemen.xyz") OR (All_Traffic.app="regasm.exe" AND All_Traffic.dest_is_internal="false") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("162.216.241.242", "198.23.185.81", "2.59.134.97") or RemoteUrl has_any ("mora1987.work.gd", "r.servermanagemen.xyz", "fileget.loseyourip.com", "direct-download.giize.com", "studioobs.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["162.216.241.242", "198.23.185.81", "2.59.134.97"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["mora1987.work.gd", "r.servermanagemen.xyz", "fileget.loseyourip.com", "direct-download.giize.com", "studioobs.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("162.216.241.242", "198.23.185.81", "2.59.134.97")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("mora1987.work.gd", "r.servermanagemen.xyz", "fileget.loseyourip.com", "direct-download.giize.com", "studioobs.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("mora1987.work.gd", "r.servermanagemen.xyz", "fileget.loseyourip.com", "direct-download.giize.com", "studioobs.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("162.216.241.242", "198.23.185.81", "2.59.134.97")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("mora1987.work.gd", "r.servermanagemen.xyz", "fileget.loseyourip.com", "direct-download.giize.com", "studioobs.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("mora1987.work.gd", "r.servermanagemen.xyz", "fileget.loseyourip.com", "direct-download.giize.com", "studioobs.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args Installation High
schtasks.exe /create or Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler EventID 4698 with LOLBin actions.
ATT&CKT1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("powershell","cmd.exe","rundll32","-enc","FromBase64","\Users\Public","\AppData\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has "/create"
| where CommandLine has_any ("powershell","cmd.exe","rundll32","-enc","FromBase64",
                              "\Users\Public", "\AppData\")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, NewProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Scheduled Task Creation with Suspicious Image / Encoded Args
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0d
status: experimental
description: |
    schtasks.exe /create with payload-shaped action — points at
    powershell, cmd, rundll32, encoded-base64, or user-writable paths.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1053.005
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_schtasks:
        Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: '/create'
    selection_payload:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'powershell'
            - 'cmd.exe'
            - 'rundll32'
            - '-enc'
            - 'FromBase64'
            - '\Users\Public'
            - '\AppData\'
    condition: selection_schtasks and selection_payload
falsepositives:
    - GPO-driven scheduled tasks, MDT/SCCM imaging
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" AND Processes.process="*/create*"
      AND (Processes.process="*powershell*" OR Processes.process="*cmd.exe*"
        OR Processes.process="*rundll32*" OR Processes.process="*-enc*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*\Users\Public*"
        OR Processes.process="*\AppData\*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" AND Processes.process="*/create*"
      AND (Processes.process="*powershell*" OR Processes.process="*cmd.exe*"
        OR Processes.process="*rundll32*" OR Processes.process="*-enc*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*\Users\Public*"
        OR Processes.process="*\AppData\*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Service install for persistence — sc.exe / new service registry write Installation High
Service install with binPath pointing to user-writeable path or LOLBin. Detects via process telemetry (sc.exe create) and registry (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\* writes).
ATT&CKT1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "sc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "create"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
// EventID 4697 is "Service installed" — direct signal, no cmdline-regex needed.
union
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4697
        | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName,
                  Detail = strcat("ServiceName=", ServiceName, " | Image=", ServiceFileName) ),
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where Account !endswith "$"
        | where NewProcessName endswith "\sc.exe" and CommandLine has "create"
        | where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account,
                  Detail = strcat("4688 sc.exe create: ", CommandLine) )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Service Persistence via sc.exe with User-Writable Path
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0e
status: experimental
description: |
    sc.exe create with the binary path under \Users\, \AppData\,
    \ProgramData\, or \Temp\ — service-install persistence outside
    legitimate program directories.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1543.003
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_sc:
        Image|endswith: '\sc.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: 'create'
    selection_path:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '\Users\'
            - '\AppData\'
            - '\ProgramData\'
            - '\Temp\'
    condition: selection_sc and selection_path
falsepositives:
    - Internal install scripts dropping a service from %ProgramData%
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name="sc.exe" AND Processes.process="*create*"
      AND (Processes.process="*\Users\*" OR Processes.process="*\AppData\*"
        OR Processes.process="*\ProgramData\*" OR Processes.process="*\Temp\*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
        where Registry.registry_path="*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*"
          AND Registry.registry_value_name="ImagePath"
          AND (Registry.registry_value_data="*\Users\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\AppData\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\Temp\*")
        by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name="sc.exe" AND Processes.process="*create*"
      AND (Processes.process="*\Users\*" OR Processes.process="*\AppData\*"
        OR Processes.process="*\ProgramData\*" OR Processes.process="*\Temp\*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
        where Registry.registry_path="*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*"
          AND Registry.registry_value_name="ImagePath"
          AND (Registry.registry_value_data="*\Users\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\AppData\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\Temp\*")
        by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`]
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("87603ea025623b19954e460add532048") or SHA1 in~ ("87603ea025623b19954e460add532048") or MD5 in~ ("87603ea025623b19954e460add532048")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("87603ea025623b19954e460add532048") or SHA1 in~ ("87603ea025623b19954e460add532048") or MD5 in~ ("87603ea025623b19954e460add532048")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["87603ea025623b19954e460add532048"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ARToken: Inside an EvilTokens affiliate panel targeting Microsoft 365

Cisco Talos
2026-07-01 16 use cases 12 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Talos has identified "ARToken," a phishing-as-a-service platform that targets Microsoft 365. The ARToken panel exposes 80+ API endpoints for device code phishing, Primary Refresh Token persistence, email access, BEC operations, and SharePoint exfiltration.

ATT&CKT1027 T1098.001 T1114.002 T1190 T1497.001 T1528 T1531 T1550.001 T1566 T1566.001 T1566.002 T1583.006
Domainspamconj.com dashboard-bl.pamconj.com spx.pamconj.com clear90489058903-document.workers.dev

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] ARToken vendor-impersonation phish: look-alike SharePoint tenant + workers.dev lure with SPF/DKIM/DMARC fail · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] EvilTokens device-code MFA bypass: successful device-code auth then token replay from a different IP · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] EvilTokens PRT persistence: Entra device registration / broker (WAM) sign-in after device-code auth · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ARToken C2/panel and Cloudflare Workers lure beaconing (pamconj.com + {uuid}-*.workers.dev) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] EvilTokens evidence suppression: malicious inbox rule (external forward / auto-delete / hide-to-RSS) · [LLM] EvilTokens SharePoint/OneDrive bulk exfiltration from a single session · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
ARToken vendor-impersonation phish: look-alike SharePoint tenant + workers.dev lure with SPF/DKIM/DMARC fail AIDelivery High
Hunts inbound mail carrying the ARToken campaign's concrete lure URLs — the folded-.com look-alike SharePoint tenant (mononapfpcom.sharepoint.com) and the Cloudflare Workers lure hosts (clear90489058903-document.workers.dev and the {uuid}-docviewer/-onedrive/-adobe2.workers.dev naming pattern) — where inbound authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC, compauth=none) fails. Article-specific because it keys on the exact impersonated tenant string and the kit's UUID-prefixed Workers subdomain convention rather than generic phishing heuristics. Rationale: Keys on the exact article IOCs — the folded look-alike tenant mononapfpcom.sharepoint.com (vs real mononapfp), the named Workers lure clear90489058903-document.workers.dev, the kit's {uuid}-docviewer/-onedrive/-adobe2.workers.dev pattern, plus the described triple auth-fail (compauth=none reason=405). sentinel_kql left empty: the listed Sentinel tables have no inbound-mail URL equivalent of EmailEvents/EmailUrlInfo in this tenant. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/new-widespread-eviltokens-kit-device-code-phishing-as-a-service-part-1/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/device-code-phishing-hits-340-microsoft.html
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1656
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate document genuinely hosted on a third-party Workers site the org already transacts with
  • Marketing/newsletter senders whose SPF fails due to misconfigured relays but link to benign SharePoint
  • Internal test phishing/awareness campaigns using look-alike domains
  • A real vendor whose DKIM temporarily breaks due to key rotation while sending SharePoint links
Suppression filter
| where SenderFromDomain !in~ ("your-known-partner1.com","your-newsletter-vendor.com")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full message (headers, Reply-To vs From domain, the anchor-text host vs actual href host) and confirm the destination is the look-alike tenant, not the real vendor tenant. 2) Contain: quarantine/soft-delete the message tenant-wide via Explorer, block the Workers host and mononapfpcom.sharepoint.com at proxy, and warn the recipient(s) not to complete any device-code prompt. 3) Hunt: check UrlClickEvents for clicks on these URLs, then pivot to SigninLogs for any device-code sign-in by clickers within the following hour (see the device-code UC).
let LookbackDays = 30d;
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| where AuthenticationDetails has "compauth=none" or (AuthenticationDetails has "spf=fail" and AuthenticationDetails has "dkim=fail")
| join kind=inner (
    EmailUrlInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where UrlDomain in~ ("mononapfpcom.sharepoint.com","clear90489058903-document.workers.dev")
        or UrlDomain matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f-]{8,}-(docviewer|onedrive|adobe2)\.workers\.dev$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, Url, UrlDomain, DeliveryAction, AuthenticationDetails
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
let LookbackDays = 30d;
EmailEvents

        or UrlDomain matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f-]{8,}-(docviewer|onedrive|adobe2)\.workers\.dev$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
  ) on NetworkMessageId

EvilTokens device-code MFA bypass: successful device-code auth then token replay from a different IP AIExploitation High
Detects the EvilTokens/ARToken credential-capture pattern where a victim completes a device-code (RFC 8628) authorization — satisfying MFA on the real Microsoft page — and the resulting token is immediately replayed by the operator from a different IP than the interactive leg. Goes beyond the generic single-event 'device code auth' rule by requiring the two-legged IP mismatch that distinguishes operator token theft from a benign device-code login on one device. Rationale: Grounded in the article's core TTP — device-code (RFC 8628) auth that fully bypasses MFA — sharpened with the cross-source-confirmed IP-mismatch-between-legs indicator so it doesn't just re-fire the existing generic device-code rule. Uses AuthenticationProcessingDetails 'Device Code' marker present on device-code sign-ins. datadog/falcon/splunk empty: Entra device-code + non-interactive token telemetry is not shipped to those platforms in this tenant. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/new-widespread-eviltokens-kit-device-code-phishing-as-a-service-part-1/ • https://research.splunk.com/cloud/d68d8732-6f7e-4ee5-a6eb-737f2b990b91/ • https://www.silverfort.com/blog/device-code-attacks-in-azure-from-exploitation-to-detection/
ATT&CKT1621 T1528
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate device-code login for a smart-TV/IoT/CLI app where the user's phone (auth leg) and the device (token leg) are on different networks
  • Roaming user on cellular during auth then corporate Wi-Fi for token use within 2h
  • Conference-room shared-device sign-ins using device code by design
  • VPN/egress-NAT changes making the same session appear from two IPs
Suppression filter
| where AuthIP !in ("<corp-egress-cidr-not-applicable>") | where DistinctTokenIPs >= 1 and TokenApps has_any ("Microsoft Authentication Broker","Microsoft Office","Office 365 Exchange Online","Office 365 SharePoint Online")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the device-code sign-in was user-initiated (call the user) and inspect the token-replay IP/ASN and app IDs for anomalies (foreign ASN, unfamiliar client_id, broker app). 2) Contain: revoke the user's refresh tokens (Revoke-AzureADUserAllRefreshToken / revokeSignInSessions), force password reset AND — because PRT survives password reset — remove any newly registered device, and block the offending IP. 3) Hunt: pivot to AuditLogs for device registrations by this user (persistence UC) and OfficeActivity for mass mail/SharePoint access from the token IP.
let Window = 2h;
let DeviceCode = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ErrorCode == 0
    | extend Details = tostring(AuthenticationProcessingDetails)
    | where Details has "Device Code"
    | project AuthTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, AuthIP = IPAddress;
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ErrorCode == 0 and IsInteractive == false
| join kind=inner DeviceCode on AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (AuthTime .. AuthTime + Window)
| where IPAddress != AuthIP
| summarize DistinctTokenIPs = dcount(IPAddress), TokenApps = make_set(Application, 10), FirstTokenUse = min(Timestamp) by AccountUpn, AuthTime, AuthIP
| order by AuthTime desc
let Window = 2h;
let DeviceCode = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ResultType == 0
    | extend Details = tostring(AuthenticationProcessingDetails)
    | where Details has "Device Code"
    | project AuthTime = TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AuthIP = IPAddress;
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ResultType == 0
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, AppDisplayName, ResourceDisplayName
| join kind=inner DeviceCode on UserPrincipalName
| where TimeGenerated between (AuthTime .. AuthTime + Window)
| where IPAddress != AuthIP
| summarize DistinctTokenIPs = dcount(IPAddress), TokenApps = make_set(AppDisplayName, 10), FirstTokenUse = min(TimeGenerated) by UserPrincipalName, AuthTime, AuthIP
| order by AuthTime desc
ARToken C2/panel and Cloudflare Workers lure beaconing (pamconj.com + {uuid}-*.workers.dev) AICommand & Control High
Hunts endpoint/DNS traffic to the ARToken C2 and management infrastructure — pamconj.com and its spx./dashboard-bl. subdomains — plus the kit's Cloudflare Workers lure hosts (clear90489058903-document.workers.dev and the {uuid}-docviewer/-onedrive/-adobe2.workers.dev pattern). Article-specific because it targets the named C2 apex and the kit's exact Workers subdomain convention, not all *.workers.dev traffic. Rationale: Uses the pre-extracted named IOCs (pamconj.com, spx./dashboard-bl. subdomains, clear90489058903-document.workers.dev) plus the article's stated {uuid}-docviewer/-onedrive/-adobe2.workers.dev naming convention. Anchoring on the specific C2 apex avoids the *.workers.dev allowlist anti-pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/artoken-inside-an-eviltokens-affiliate-panel-targeting-microsoft-365/
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A benign internal app coincidentally hosted on a {uuid}-onedrive.workers.dev-style dev subdomain
  • Security researchers/analysts sandbox-detonating the lure from a corporate host
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling resolving the IOC domains for feeds
  • Proxy/DNS logging replay during IOC block-list testing
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the resolving host and the initiating process (browser vs scripting/LOLBin) and whether resolution led to an actual connection. 2) Contain: sinkhole/block pamconj.com and the Workers hosts at DNS+proxy, and isolate the host if a non-browser process initiated the lookup. 3) Hunt: correlate the resolving user to SigninLogs device-code events and to inbound mail carrying these URLs (initial-access UC) to scope who clicked.
let LookbackDays = 30d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl endswith "pamconj.com"
    or RemoteUrl =~ "clear90489058903-document.workers.dev"
    or RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f-]{8,}-(docviewer|onedrive|adobe2)\.workers\.dev$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name endswith "pamconj.com"
    or Name =~ "clear90489058903-document.workers.dev"
    or Name matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f-]{8,}-(docviewer|onedrive|adobe2)\.workers\.dev$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, QueryTypeName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

EvilTokens PRT persistence: Entra device registration / broker (WAM) sign-in after device-code auth AIInstallation Medium
Detects the EvilTokens/ARToken persistence chain where captured tokens are escalated to a Primary Refresh Token by registering a device via Microsoft's Authentication Broker (WAM, the clientMode:"broker" flow) shortly after a device-code sign-in. This is the platform's core differentiator (survives password reset), so it warrants its own pivot separate from the initial credential capture. Rationale: Targets the article's /prt/setup->/prt/refresh->/prt/cookie persistence chain via its observable Entra footprint: device registration and the Microsoft Authentication Broker app (AppId 29d9ed98-a469-4536-ade2-f981bc1d605e) that clientMode:"broker"/WAM uses, correlated to a preceding device-code sign-in. Splunk/CloudWatch empty: no CIM/AWS home for Entra directory audit here. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/new-widespread-eviltokens-kit-device-code-phishing-as-a-service-part-1/ • https://www.silverfort.com/blog/device-code-attacks-in-azure-from-exploitation-to-detection/
ATT&CKT1098.005 T1606.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate new-device onboarding / Windows Autopilot enrollment right after a device-code login
  • BYOD device registration by a user who genuinely used device code on a shared machine
  • Helpdesk-assisted device join within the 6h window
  • MDM re-enrollment following a wipe
Suppression filter
| where ActorIP != AuthIP
Response runbook
1) Triage: verify with the user whether they registered a new device; inspect the registered device name, join type, and the ActorIP/AuthIP for foreign ASN. 2) Contain: disable/delete the attacker-registered device object, revoke the user's tokens AND the PRT (a password reset alone will not evict the PRT), and apply Conditional Access to require compliant device. 3) Hunt: review AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs for continued token renewal after the reset, and OfficeActivity for mailbox/SharePoint access from the device.
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ApplicationId == "29d9ed98-a469-4536-ade2-f981bc1d605e"   // Microsoft Authentication Broker (WAM) — clientMode:"broker" PRT acquisition
| where ErrorCode == 0
| extend Details = tostring(AuthenticationProcessingDetails)
| where Details has "Device Code" or IsInteractive == false
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Application, IPAddress, Country, DeviceTrustType, AadDeviceId, IsInteractive
| order by Timestamp desc
let DeviceCode = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ResultType == 0
    | extend Details = tostring(AuthenticationProcessingDetails)
    | where Details has "Device Code"
    | project AuthTime = TimeGenerated, Actor = tolower(UserPrincipalName), AuthIP = IPAddress;
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where OperationName in ("Add device","Register device","Add registered owner to device","Add registered user to device")
| where Result == "success"
| extend Actor = tolower(tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)), ActorIP = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| mv-apply tr = TargetResources on (extend TargetName = tostring(tr.displayName))
| project RegTime = TimeGenerated, Actor, ActorIP, OperationName, TargetName
| join kind=inner DeviceCode on Actor
| where RegTime between (AuthTime .. AuthTime + 6h)
| project AuthTime, RegTime, Actor, AuthIP, ActorIP, OperationName, TargetName
| order by RegTime desc
source:azure.activeDirectory (@evt.name:"Add device" OR @evt.name:"Register device" OR @evt.name:"Add registered owner to device")
EvilTokens evidence suppression: malicious inbox rule (external forward / auto-delete / hide-to-RSS) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the ARToken operator capability of programmatically creating inbox rules that forward mail externally or hide it (move to Deleted Items / RSS Feeds, delete message) to suppress evidence of BEC and token theft. Article-specific to the panel's 'Inbox rule manipulation' feature used post-compromise on stolen-token sessions. Rationale: Maps to the panel's documented 'Inbox rule manipulation ... for evidence suppression' capability by inspecting inbox-rule creation for external-forward and hide-to-Deleted/RSS parameters — the exact behaviours the kit automates on compromised mailboxes. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/artoken-inside-an-eviltokens-affiliate-panel-targeting-microsoft-365/ • https://blog.sekoia.io/new-widespread-eviltokens-kit-device-code-phishing-as-a-service-part-1/
ATT&CKT1564.008 T1114.003
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User legitimately sets up forwarding to a personal/archive address
  • Admin-created mail flow / journaling rules
  • Out-of-office or organizational rules moving newsletters to a folder
  • Third-party mailbox add-in creating rules during setup
Suppression filter
| where Params !has "@yourcorp.com"
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the rule's exact conditions/actions and the ClientIP that created it; forwarding to an external free-mail domain or auto-deleting invoice-keyword mail is high signal. 2) Contain: remove the malicious rule, revoke the session/tokens for the creating identity, and block external auto-forwarding at the transport level. 3) Hunt: correlate the ClientIP to device-code sign-ins and to bulk SharePoint/mailbox access, and search for send-as BEC mail referencing invoices/banking changes.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","UpdateInboxRules")
| extend Raw = tostring(RawEventData)
| where Raw has_any ("ForwardTo","ForwardAsAttachmentTo","RedirectTo","DeleteMessage")
    or (Raw has "MoveToFolder" and Raw has_any ("Deleted Items","RSS","RSS Feeds","Conversation History","Archive"))
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountId, IPAddress, ActionType, Application, Raw
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Operation in ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","UpdateInboxRules")
| extend Params = tostring(Parameters)
| where Params has_any ("ForwardTo","ForwardAsAttachmentTo","RedirectTo","DeleteMessage")
    or (Params has "MoveToFolder" and Params has_any ("Deleted Items","RSS","RSS Feeds","Conversation History","Archive"))
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Operation, OfficeWorkload, Params
| order by TimeGenerated desc
EvilTokens SharePoint/OneDrive bulk exfiltration from a single session AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects large-volume SharePoint/OneDrive file downloads by one identity from one client IP in a short window — the ARToken panel's 'Full SharePoint operations' / SharePoint-exfiltration capability executed with stolen tokens. Distinct pivot from the C2 and mail-based UCs: it targets the collection/exfil fan-out on document repositories. Rationale: Targets the panel's documented SharePoint/OneDrive file download-and-exfil capability via a per-identity/per-IP hourly download fan-out threshold, the cleanest signal of token-driven bulk document theft. Threshold commented for tuning per anti-magic-numbers guidance. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/artoken-inside-an-eviltokens-affiliate-panel-targeting-microsoft-365/
ATT&CKT1213.002 T1114.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • OneDrive/SharePoint sync client performing a full initial sync on a new device
  • Legitimate site migration or bulk export by a records/IT team
  • Data-science/BI user pulling many files for analysis
  • eDiscovery or backup tooling downloading at scale
Suppression filter
| where ClientIP !in ("<corp-sync-egress-not-applicable>") | where not (Files has_any (".aspx"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: check whether the download burst came from a sync client vs a browser/API session and whether the ClientIP matches the user's normal geo/ASN or a token-replay IP. 2) Contain: revoke tokens for the identity, suspend the session, and restrict external sharing on the affected sites. 3) Hunt: correlate the ClientIP to device-code sign-ins and inbox-rule creation, and review whether downloaded files were re-uploaded/shared externally for lateral phishing.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application in ("Microsoft SharePoint Online","Microsoft OneDrive for Business")
| where ActionType in ("FileDownloaded","FileSyncDownloadedFull")
| summarize FileCount = dcount(ObjectName), Files = make_set(ObjectName, 20), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where FileCount > 50    // 50 = bulk-download threshold; tune to org P95 of hourly per-user downloads
| order by FileCount desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload in ("SharePoint","OneDrive")
| where Operation in ("FileDownloaded","FileSyncDownloadedFull")
| summarize FileCount = dcount(SourceFileName), Files = make_set(SourceFileName, 20), Sites = make_set(Site_Url, 10), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by UserId, ClientIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where FileCount > 50    // 50 = bulk-download threshold; tune to org P95 of hourly per-user downloads
| order by FileCount desc
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

Phantom Squatting Uses AI-Hallucinated Domains for Phishing and Malware

The Hacker News
2026-07-01 10 use cases 6 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Large language models keep inventing web addresses that do not exist. Attackers have started buying those made-up domains before anyone else can, then hosting phishing pages on them to catch traffic that AI tools point their way. Palo Alto Networks'&nbsp;Unit 42&nbsp;calls the trick phantom squatting, and its new research shows it is already happening in the wild. The reason it matters is

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Montana Empire phishing-kit ZIP / postal-service APK file hash on endpoint · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Victim traffic to Montana Empire phishing-kit endpoints (/mentalite.php, /panel_track.php, /verify_api.php, /letgovip.zip) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Montana Empire phishing-kit ZIP / postal-service APK file hash on endpoint AIDelivery Medium
Hunts endpoints that write or download the two Unit 42-confirmed Phantom Squatting artifacts: the Montana Empire phishing-kit ZIP (SHA256 eb07edaa…, 7,958,528 bytes) and the malicious postal-service Android APK (SHA256 2202a30d…, 12,649,472 bytes). Article-specific because it pins exact corroborated hashes rather than a generic 'suspicious download' pattern. Rationale: Uses the two SHA256 hashes and exact file sizes (7,958,528-byte ZIP kit, 12,649,472-byte APK) published in Unit 42's primary report and cross-checked against the hendryadrian mirror; exact-hash matching is inherently high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/phantom-squatting-hallucinated-web-domains/ • https://x.com/Unit42_Intel/status/2041879323963982303 • https://www.hendryadrian.com/phantom-squatting-ai-hallucinated-domains-as-a-software-supply-chain-vector/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC/IR analyst intentionally downloading the sample from MalwareBazaar/VirusTotal for analysis
  • Automated malware-detonation sandbox host writing the sample to disk
  • Threat-intel platform syncing IOC sample repositories to a research share
  • Red-team exercise staging the kit for a phishing-simulation replica
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ ("IR-SANDBOX01","MALWARE-LAB01") and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("vmtoolsd.exe","cuckoo.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm the hash match and inspect FileOriginUrl/InitiatingProcess to determine if the file arrived via browser download, email attachment, or file share, and whether the host is an analyst/sandbox box (expected) or a standard user endpoint (unexpected). Step 2 — Contain: on a non-analyst endpoint, isolate the device, quarantine the file, and reset any credentials/payment data entered on the associated phishing domain. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on FileOriginUrl/RemoteUrl to identify the phantom domain, then sweep the org for other hosts contacting that host or the kit's PHP endpoints (see companion UC), and check EmailAttachmentInfo for the same SHA256.

Victim traffic to Montana Empire phishing-kit endpoints (/mentalite.php, /panel_track.php, /verify_api.php, /letgovip.zip) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts endpoints whose browser or an AI agent reaches the distinctive server-side paths of the Montana Empire kit, where card numbers, IBANs, national IDs and OTPs are captured and relayed to the operator's Telegram panel. Article-specific because it keys on the kit's actual PHP filenames rather than generic phishing heuristics. Rationale: Uses the four distinctive kit paths (/mentalite.php, /panel_track.php, /verify_api.php, /letgovip.zip) enumerated in Unit 42's Montana Empire teardown; /mentalite.php and /letgovip.zip are highly non-generic, so co-occurrence with the two /*_api endpoints is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/phantom-squatting-hallucinated-web-domains/ • https://x.com/Unit42_Intel/status/2041879323963982303
ATT&CKT1056.003 T1566.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate internal or SaaS app that happens to expose a generically-named /verify_api.php or /panel_track.php endpoint
  • Security scanner or web crawler enumerating .php paths across many hosts
  • Red-team phishing-simulation infrastructure mirroring the kit paths
  • DAST/pentest tooling probing arbitrary PHP endpoints during an authorized assessment
Suppression filter
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/mentalite.php","/letgovip.zip") or (RemoteUrl has_any ("/panel_track.php","/verify_api.php") and RemoteIPType == "Public")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm the RemoteUrl/DstHostname is an external, recently-registered domain impersonating a postal service, bank, or betting brand (not an internal app), and check which user/process initiated the request. Step 2 — Contain: block the domain/IP at proxy and DNS, and if the user reached /panel_track.php or /verify_api.php, treat any payment card, IBAN, national ID, or OTP they entered as compromised and initiate card reissue / account lockdown. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the destination host to find all other org users who touched it, correlate with the file-hash UC for the dropped APK, and query newly-observed domains resolving to the same IP to surface sibling phantom domains.

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
