Cryptojacker security-control teardown: mass pkill of rival miners + firewall/LSM disable AIInstallation High
Hunts the lambsys defense-evasion cascade: dozens of sh -c subprocesses running pkill against Kinsing/WatchDog/Rocke/Outlaw and disabling AppArmor, ufw, iptables, SELinux, the NMI watchdog and the Aliyun agent. Article-specific via the named rival families and the exact controls disabled. Rationale: Uses the article's named rival families (Kinsing, WatchDog, Rocke, Outlaw) and the exact controls lambsys disables (AppArmor, ufw, iptables, SELinux, NMI watchdog, Aliyun agent). The >5 threshold reflects the described cascade of ~51 short-lived pkill/chattr/sysctl subprocesses.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1562.004 T1489
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin hardening or firewall-migration scripts that stop ufw/iptables during a maintenance window
  • Config-management runs (Ansible/Chef) that toggle SELinux/AppArmor across a fleet
  • Alibaba Cloud agent uninstall during a legitimate cloud migration
  • AV/EDR product removing a genuine Kinsing infection (would show its own vendor binary as parent)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("ansible","chef-client","puppet","cloud-init")
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the full set of child commands under the single parent PID — a single process firing pkill + setenforce + ufw disable + aliyun-kill in seconds is not admin activity. 2) Contain: isolate host, re-enable AppArmor/SELinux/ufw, kill the parent process tree. 3) Hunt: look for the lambsys binary, cron persistence, and the miner beacon on the same host; check whether host security agents were tampered with.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("pkill","systemctl","service","setenforce","ufw","aa-teardown","sysctl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("kinsing","kdevtmpfsi","watchdog","apparmor","ufw disable","iptables","setenforce 0","nmi_watchdog","aliyun","AliYunDun","selinux")
| summarize CmdCount = count(), Cmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 60), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AccountName
| where CmdCount > 5   // lambsys forks ~51 short-lived pkill/chattr/sysctl children per run
| order by LastSeen desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("pkill","setenforce 0","ufw disable","systemctl stop apparmor","iptables -F","nmi_watchdog","aliyun","AliYunDun")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("kinsing","kdevtmpfsi","watchdog","apparmor","iptables","selinux","aliyun")
| summarize CmdCount = count(), Cmds = make_set(SyslogMessage, 60) by Computer, HostIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where CmdCount > 5
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.name:pkill OR @process.name:setenforce OR @process.name:ufw OR @process.name:systemctl OR @process.name:sysctl) (@process.command_line:*kinsing* OR @process.command_line:*kdevtmpfsi* OR @process.command_line:*apparmor* OR @process.command_line:*"ufw disable"* OR @process.command_line:*"setenforce 0"* OR @process.command_line:*nmi_watchdog* OR @process.command_line:*aliyun* OR @process.command_line:*AliYunDun*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(pkill|setenforce|ufw|systemctl|sysctl|service)$/i | regex("(kinsing|kdevtmpfsi|watchdog|apparmor|ufw disable|setenforce 0|iptables|nmi_watchdog|aliyun|AliYunDun|selinux)", field=CommandLine) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=count()) | count > 5
ENDPOINT

lambsys immutable-flag manipulation on cron/ld.so.preload/SSH persistence paths AIInstallation High
Detects the chattr -i / chattr +i sequence lambsys uses to unlock and re-lock persistence-critical files (~/.ssh, authorized_keys, /etc/crontab, /etc/ld.so.preload, /tmp, /var/tmp, /var/spool/cron). Article-specific via the exact file set and the +i re-lock of /tmp and /var/tmp. Rationale: The article lists the precise files lambsys unlocks/relocks with chattr (~/.ssh, authorized_keys, /etc/crontab, /etc/ld.so.preload, /tmp, /var/tmp, /var/spool/cron) and notes it re-applies +i to /tmp and /var/tmp — a rare, high-fidelity persistence-hardening behaviour.
ATT&CKT1222.002 T1546.008 T1053.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Hardening frameworks (CIS benchmark scripts) that set +i on /etc/crontab or ld.so.preload
  • A sysadmin protecting authorized_keys with chattr +i as a deliberate control
  • Backup tooling temporarily clearing immutable flags to restore files
  • Another cryptominer family using the same chattr technique (still malicious — triage accordingly)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("cis-","hardening","ansible","restore")
Response runbook
1) Triage: dump the chattr target list and the parent process; a single process chattr-ing ld.so.preload + cron + .ssh in sequence is malicious. 2) Contain: isolate host; run `lsattr` on the listed paths, remove attacker +i flags, inspect /etc/ld.so.preload and /var/spool/cron for injected entries, rotate exposed SSH keys. 3) Hunt: pivot on the parent (lambsys/shell) and enumerate SSH-reachable hosts for lateral spread.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "chattr"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ld.so.preload","/var/spool/cron","/etc/crontab","authorized_keys",".ssh","/tmp","/var/tmp")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("+i","-i")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has "chattr"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("ld.so.preload","/var/spool/cron","/etc/crontab","authorized_keys",".ssh")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("+i","-i")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

lambsys C2 beacon to 83.142.209.214 / 94.156.64.241 and ipinfo.io geolocation lookup AICommand & Control Medium
Detects outbound connections to the campaign C2 (83.142.209.214:80, 94.156.64.241) used to fetch the shell script, miner binary and XMRig TAR, plus the ipinfo.io lookup lambsys performs for pool-selection/geo-fencing. Article-specific via the hardcoded C2 IPs and ipinfo.io usage. Rationale: 83.142.209.214:80 is the article's explicit beacon/download server and 94.156.64.241 is a pre-extracted campaign IP; ipinfo.io is the named geolocation service used for pool selection and geo-fencing. Hardcoded IOCs make this alerting-grade.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1614
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate apps calling ipinfo.io for geolocation (common in analytics SDKs) — the IP hits are the strong signal, ipinfo.io alone is weaker
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling deliberately resolving the C2 IPs in a sandbox
  • Security scanners connecting to the IPs for confirmation
  • Shared-hosting reuse if the C2 IP is later reassigned (validate timestamp against the Mar27–Apr15 2026 window)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process for the C2 IP connections — if it is lambsys/curl/wget under a Langflow host, treat as confirmed. 2) Contain: block 83.142.209.214 and 94.156.64.241 at the egress firewall, isolate the host, kill the beaconing process. 3) Hunt: sweep all internet-facing Langflow hosts for connections to these IPs and to mining-pool infrastructure; confirm CVE-2026-33017 patch status.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("83.142.209.214","94.156.64.241") or RemoteUrl has "ipinfo.io"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP in ("83.142.209.214","94.156.64.241") or DestinationHostName has "ipinfo.io" or RequestURL has "ipinfo.io"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, ApplicationProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

XMRig Monero miner execution and mining-pool Stratum egress on Langflow hosts AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the final-stage bespoke XMRig miner: execution by name/args (--donate-level, stratum+tcp, cryptonight, -o pool) and outbound Stratum connections on common pool ports (3333/5555/7777/9999/14444). Scopes to server/Langflow hosts to catch the resource-hijacking impact. Article-specific via the named XMRig payload delivered by lambsys. Rationale: The article states lambsys extracts and runs a bespoke XMRig miner as its final stage. XMRig binary name and its distinctive Stratum/RandomX/--donate-level arguments are the highest-fidelity, deployment-agnostic indicators of the Monero-mining impact described.
ATT&CKT1496 T1071
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sanctioned in-house mining / benchmarking on a dev box (rare on a Langflow app server)
  • Security research reproducing XMRig in a lab
  • A monitoring agent whose config string legitimately contains 'randomx' or 'cryptonight' (unlikely)
  • Password-cracking or crypto-benchmark tools sharing RandomX libraries
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName in (SecurityServerList) == false
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the parent chain leads back to lambsys/Langflow and extract the -o pool address and wallet from the command line. 2) Contain: kill the xmrig process, isolate the host, block the mining-pool destination, and preserve the binary before it self-wipes. 3) Hunt: correlate with the C2 IPs and cron persistence on the same host, and check all Langflow endpoints for CVE-2026-33017 exploitation and reused-SSH-key lateral movement.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "xmrig"
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("stratum+tcp","--donate-level","cryptonight","--coin monero","randomx","--cpu-priority")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("xmrig","stratum+tcp","--donate-level","cryptonight","randomx","--coin monero")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33017")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33017")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("71af8bd9b8019b7e5f460ce4c5c14ff7716a2c2faaaf1f274ceaa54cb89723bc", "33588aa446984d3340cab686d38f2aa85a70eb3f76c459da3eef0304592b99df", "ddde47bf00324075c7eeb0b9d0ff0a5d1b95bfc619aca4b5def85263838212f2", "46096a72d84db5f1dafd944fcf6571c8") or SHA1 in~ ("71af8bd9b8019b7e5f460ce4c5c14ff7716a2c2faaaf1f274ceaa54cb89723bc", "33588aa446984d3340cab686d38f2aa85a70eb3f76c459da3eef0304592b99df", "ddde47bf00324075c7eeb0b9d0ff0a5d1b95bfc619aca4b5def85263838212f2", "46096a72d84db5f1dafd944fcf6571c8") or MD5 in~ ("71af8bd9b8019b7e5f460ce4c5c14ff7716a2c2faaaf1f274ceaa54cb89723bc", "33588aa446984d3340cab686d38f2aa85a70eb3f76c459da3eef0304592b99df", "ddde47bf00324075c7eeb0b9d0ff0a5d1b95bfc619aca4b5def85263838212f2", "46096a72d84db5f1dafd944fcf6571c8")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("71af8bd9b8019b7e5f460ce4c5c14ff7716a2c2faaaf1f274ceaa54cb89723bc", "33588aa446984d3340cab686d38f2aa85a70eb3f76c459da3eef0304592b99df", "ddde47bf00324075c7eeb0b9d0ff0a5d1b95bfc619aca4b5def85263838212f2", "46096a72d84db5f1dafd944fcf6571c8") or SHA1 in~ ("71af8bd9b8019b7e5f460ce4c5c14ff7716a2c2faaaf1f274ceaa54cb89723bc", "33588aa446984d3340cab686d38f2aa85a70eb3f76c459da3eef0304592b99df", "ddde47bf00324075c7eeb0b9d0ff0a5d1b95bfc619aca4b5def85263838212f2", "46096a72d84db5f1dafd944fcf6571c8") or MD5 in~ ("71af8bd9b8019b7e5f460ce4c5c14ff7716a2c2faaaf1f274ceaa54cb89723bc", "33588aa446984d3340cab686d38f2aa85a70eb3f76c459da3eef0304592b99df", "ddde47bf00324075c7eeb0b9d0ff0a5d1b95bfc619aca4b5def85263838212f2", "46096a72d84db5f1dafd944fcf6571c8")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["71af8bd9b8019b7e5f460ce4c5c14ff7716a2c2faaaf1f274ceaa54cb89723bc", "33588aa446984d3340cab686d38f2aa85a70eb3f76c459da3eef0304592b99df", "ddde47bf00324075c7eeb0b9d0ff0a5d1b95bfc619aca4b5def85263838212f2", "46096a72d84db5f1dafd944fcf6571c8"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — Langflow RCE Exploited to Deploy Monero Miner on Exposed AI App Endpoints Installation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Langflow RCE Exploited to Deploy Monero Miner on Exposed AI App Endpoints
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/etc/crontab", "/etc/ld.so.preload", "/var/tmp/", "/var/spool/cron", "/var/tmp/."))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Malicious 'Perplexity AI' Chromium extension flkebkiofojicogddingbdmcmkpbplcd written to browser profile · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Browser egress to fake-Perplexity interception infra (perplexity-ai.online / oda.digital / extension.tilda.ws) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Malicious 'Perplexity AI' Chromium extension flkebkiofojicogddingbdmcmkpbplcd written to browser profile AIInstallation High
Hunts the on-disk install of the fake 'Search for perplexity ai' extension by its globally-unique Chrome Web Store ID landing in a Chromium browser's Extensions folder. Article-specific because the ID flkebkiofojicogddingbdmcmkpbplcd is the single highest-fidelity IOC Microsoft published. Rationale: Pivots on the unique extension ID flkebkiofojicogddingbdmcmkpbplcd (Microsoft IOC, cross-checked against the MS Security blog and The Hacker News); a Chromium browser writing this folder name to a profile is unambiguous and needs no thresholding. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/29/chromium-extension-uses-airelated-branding-redirect-browser-search/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/malicious-perplexity-chrome-extension.html • https://www.csoonline.com/article/4191060/malicious-chromium-extension-spoofs-perplexity-ai-to-hijack-browser-searches.html
ATT&CKT1176.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher or IR analyst intentionally detonating/analyzing the extension sample on a sandbox host
  • DFIR tooling copying a captured browser profile (which contains the ID folder) onto an analyst workstation
  • Chrome profile sync restoring an old profile snapshot that still contains the extension before it was pulled from the store
  • EDR/AV quarantine relocating the extension folder, generating a file-write event under the ID
Suppression filter
| where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the device + user, and check the parent browser process and folder timestamp to see when the extension was sideloaded; confirm extension still present in chrome://extensions. 2) Contain: remove the extension by ID flkebkiofojicogddingbdmcmkpbplcd from the user's browser, reset default search provider, and force-rotate the user's critical-account passwords per Microsoft guidance. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2 to confirm the host ever beaconed to perplexity-ai.online/oda.digital, and sweep all endpoints for the same ID folder to scope org-wide spread.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "flkebkiofojicogddingbdmcmkpbplcd"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","vivaldi.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "flkebkiofojicogddingbdmcmkpbplcd"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Browser egress to fake-Perplexity interception infra (perplexity-ai.online / oda.digital / extension.tilda.ws) AICommand & Control High
Hunts a browser resolving/connecting to the typosquatted search-interception domain perplexity-ai.online, the operator domain oda.digital, or the onboarding page extension.tilda.ws used by the fake Perplexity extension. Article-specific because these exact domains carry the intercepted Omnibox queries and keystroke-level suggest_url traffic. Rationale: Uses the three exact domains Microsoft published (perplexity-ai.online = query/suggest_url interception endpoint, oda.digital = operator infra, extension.tilda.ws = onboarding); a browser touching perplexity-ai.online in particular is a clean true positive since the legitimate service is perplexity.ai. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/29/chromium-extension-uses-airelated-branding-redirect-browser-search/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/malicious-perplexity-chrome-extension.html
ATT&CKT1176.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A user legitimately browsing an unrelated site hosted on Tilda's website builder under the shared extension.tilda.ws subdomain
  • oda.digital resolving for an unrelated benign service that happens to share the name
  • Threat-intel/sandbox detonation host deliberately visiting these domains during analysis
  • Security awareness/phishing-simulation platform replaying the IOC domains as part of a test
Suppression filter
| where RemoteUrl has "perplexity-ai.online"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host/user and the initiating browser; confirm whether the resolution targeted perplexity-ai.online (high confidence) vs oda.digital/extension.tilda.ws (verify context), and check timing against the extension install. 2) Contain: remove extension flkebkiofojicogddingbdmcmkpbplcd, reset default search provider, and block the three domains at proxy/DNS. 3) Hunt: correlate with UC1 file-write to confirm install on the same host, enumerate every internal host resolving perplexity-ai.online to scope, and rotate passwords for accounts whose searches may have been logged.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("perplexity-ai.online","oda.digital","extension.tilda.ws")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","vivaldi.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has_any ("perplexity-ai.online","oda.digital","extension.tilda.ws")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Non-browser process writing Chromium 'Secure Preferences'/'Preferences' (Silent Swap sideload) · [LLM] Single process force-terminating multiple Chromium browsers (Silent Swap profile-unlock precursor) · Suspicious browser extension installation · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Silent Swap / VPN Go clipper C2 and clipboard-exfil to known infrastructure · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Non-browser process writing Chromium 'Secure Preferences'/'Preferences' (Silent Swap sideload) AIInstallation High
Hunts the Silent Swap covert extension install: a non-browser process (the unsigned .NET BaseZipInstaller or Golang variant) writing to a Chromium 'Secure Preferences' or 'Preferences' file under a browser User Data profile. Normally only the browser itself writes these HMAC-protected files; a third-party writer indicates the malware tampering with protected settings to silently register the fake 'Google Notes' extension. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit covert-install mechanic: the malware modifies the browser's HMAC-protected 'Secure Preferences'/'Preferences' files (under User Data) from a non-browser installer. Limiting the writer to non-browser processes makes this very high-fidelity since legit modification is browser-exclusive. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/silent-swap-crypto-clipper-uses-fake.html • https://www.cse.chalmers.se/~andrei/cans20.pdf
ATT&CKT1176.001 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Browser profile migration/sync tools (e.g. third-party bookmark importers) writing Preferences
  • Enterprise browser management/GPO agents pushing managed extension policy
  • Antivirus or backup software touching the User Data folder and re-writing Preferences
  • Browser repair/reset utilities run by IT support
  • Roaming-profile redirection writing Preferences on logon
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","vivaldi.exe","opera.exe","opera_gx.exe","update.exe","software_reporter_tool.exe","googleupdate.exe","elevation_service.exe","setup.exe","msiexec.exe") or InitiatingProcessAccountName endswith "$")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName/SHA256 and FolderPath; check if the writer is signed and known. Pull the modified 'Secure Preferences' and diff the 'extensions.settings' / 'extensions.ui.developer_mode' nodes for an unfamiliar extension ID claiming 'Google Notes'. 2) Contain: kill the installer process, isolate the host, and remove the rogue extension from every Chromium profile; reset Secure Preferences. Treat any crypto wallet addresses copied during the window as compromised. 3) Hunt: pivot on the writer's SHA256 across the fleet, check for self-deleted installers and ZIP retrievals, and look for the C2 connections in UC3.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("Secure Preferences","Preferences")
| where FolderPath has @"\User Data\"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\", @"\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\", @"\Vivaldi\", @"\Opera Software\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","vivaldi.exe","opera.exe","opera_gx.exe","update.exe","software_reporter_tool.exe","googleupdate.exe","elevation_service.exe","setup.exe","msiexec.exe","msedge_proxy.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Secure Preferences","Preferences")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\User Data\"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\", @"\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\", @"\Vivaldi\", @"\Opera Software\")
| where not(ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","vivaldi.exe","opera.exe","opera_gx.exe","update.exe","software_reporter_tool.exe","googleupdate.exe","elevation_service.exe","setup.exe","msiexec.exe"))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7b3e9c2a-1d4f-4a8b-9c6e-2f5a8d1b4c30
status: experimental
description: Detects a non-browser process writing to a Chromium 'Secure Preferences' or 'Preferences' file, the covert extension-injection + HMAC-recalculation technique used by the Silent Swap crypto clipper to register a fake Google Notes extension.
references:

Single process force-terminating multiple Chromium browsers (Silent Swap profile-unlock precursor) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the Silent Swap pre-injection step where the installer enumerates installed Chromium browsers and forcibly terminates each one to unlock the profile files before tampering. Flags a single non-browser initiator running taskkill against two or more distinct Chromium browser binaries within a short window. Rationale: Built on the article's stated behaviour that the installer 'forcibly terminates the browser process' for each detected Chromium profile before modifying its files. Requiring >=2 distinct browser targets from one initiator separates this from a normal single-browser restart. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/silent-swap-crypto-clipper-uses-fake.html
ATT&CKT1176.001 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT scripts that close all browsers before a software update or imaging
  • Browser updater/installer killing the running instance before applying an update
  • User-run cleanup batch files that taskkill multiple browsers
  • Endpoint management tools (SCCM/Intune) terminating browsers for forced updates
  • RMM agents closing browsers prior to maintenance
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Program Files\", @"\Program Files (x86)\") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("update.exe","setup.exe","intunemanagementextension.exe","ccmexec.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the initiating process and parent of taskkill; legit cases trace to known updaters/RMM. Confirm whether a 'Secure Preferences' write (UC1) followed on the same host within minutes. 2) Contain: if the killer is an unknown/unsigned binary, isolate the host and capture the binary before it self-deletes. 3) Hunt: pivot on the initiator hash, search for ZIP downloads and self-deletion (file delete of own image), and check UC3 C2 connections for that host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "taskkill.exe"
| extend BrowserKilled = tolower(extract(@"(?i)(chrome|msedge|brave|vivaldi|opera|opera_gx)\.exe", 1, ProcessCommandLine))
| where isnotempty(BrowserKilled)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize KilledBrowsers = make_set(BrowserKilled), KillCount = dcount(BrowserKilled), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SampleCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 8) by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where KillCount >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\taskkill.exe"
| extend BrowserKilled = tolower(extract(@"(?i)(chrome|msedge|brave|vivaldi|opera|opera_gx)\.exe", 1, CommandLine))
| where isnotempty(BrowserKilled)
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| summarize KilledBrowsers = make_set(BrowserKilled), KillCount = dcount(BrowserKilled), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), SampleCmds = make_set(CommandLine, 8) by Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where KillCount >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 @Image:(*\\taskkill.exe OR *\\TASKKILL.EXE) @CommandLine:(*chrome.exe* OR *msedge.exe* OR *brave.exe* OR *vivaldi.exe* OR *opera.exe*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\taskkill\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(?<Browser>chrome|msedge|brave|vivaldi|opera)\.exe", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName], function=[count(field=Browser, distinct=true, as=DistinctBrowsers), collect([Browser])])
| DistinctBrowsers >= 2
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Processes.process) as process_cmds min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="taskkill.exe" (Processes.process="*chrome.exe*" OR Processes.process="*msedge.exe*" OR Processes.process="*brave.exe*" OR Processes.process="*vivaldi.exe*" OR Processes.process="*opera.exe*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name _time span=10m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| rex max_match=0 field=process_cmds "(?i)(?<browsers>chrome|msedge|brave|vivaldi|opera)\.exe"
| eval distinct_browsers=mvcount(mvdedup(browsers))
| where distinct_browsers>=2
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as process_cmds min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="taskkill.exe" (Processes.process="*chrome.exe*" OR Processes.process="*msedge.exe*" OR Processes.process="*brave.exe*" OR Processes.process="*vivaldi.exe*" OR Processes.process="*opera.exe*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name _time span=10m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| rex max_match=0 field=process_cmds "(?i)(?<browsers>chrome|msedge|brave|vivaldi|opera)\.exe"
| eval distinct_browsers=mvcount(mvdedup(browsers))
| where distinct_browsers>=2
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
Silent Swap / VPN Go clipper C2 and clipboard-exfil to known infrastructure AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on host connections to the confirmed Silent Swap and 'VPN Go' clipboard-stealer infrastructure: the two exfiltration IPs (178.236.252.133, 77.91.123.187) and the Silent Swap C2/dead-drop domain set. The campaign uses EtherHiding (blockchain dead-drop resolver) to rotate live C2, so these named IOCs are the durable network pivot for backend wallet-substitution and clipboard exfil. Rationale: Uses the two exfil IPs stated in the article body (Socket's VPN Go finding) and the McAfee Silent Swap C2 domain set. EtherHiding rotates the live C2, so direct-IP plus the static domain list is the most durable network pivot; 'bucket-aws-s*' domains are attacker C2, not real AWS, so no CloudWatch query applies. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/silent-swap-crypto-clipper-uses-fake.html • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/unc5142-etherhiding-distribute-malware
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.001 T1657
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • An exfil IP later reassigned to shared/CDN hosting serving benign traffic
  • Security tooling or sandbox detonating a sample and contacting the IOC IP
  • Threat-intel/research workstations intentionally resolving the C2 domains
  • A look-alike domain typo coincidentally matching a benign service
  • Proxy/egress appliance pre-fetching URLs for inspection
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msmpeng.exe","sense.exe","wireshark.exe") and DeviceName !has "sandbox"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess making the connection and whether it is a browser (extension-driven exfil) or the installer. Confirm the host also shows UC1/UC2 activity. 2) Contain: block the IPs/domains at the proxy/firewall, isolate the host, and remove the rogue extension; rotate any secrets/seed phrases and warn the user that copied wallet addresses may have been swapped. 3) Hunt: sweep DNS/proxy logs org-wide for the full domain list, pivot on the connecting process hash, and check for blockchain RPC traffic indicative of EtherHiding dead-drop resolution.
let c2_ips = dynamic(["178.236.252.133","77.91.123.187"]);
let c2_domains = dynamic(["hell1-kitty.cc","alphazero1-endscape.cc","api-microservice-us1.com","bucket-aws-s1.com","bucket-aws-s2.com","fileless-storage-s3.cc","globalsnn1-new.cc","globalsnn2-new.cc","globalsnn3-new.cc","handle-me-sv1.com","hardware-office.cc","health-smooth-eu1.com","health-smooth-eu2.com","health-smooth-eu3.com","holiday-updateservice.com","memory-protection-layer1.cc","memory-protection-layer2.cc","microservice-update-s1-bucket.cc","microservice-update-s2-bucket.cc","my-smart-house1.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (c2_ips) or RemoteUrl has_any (c2_domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2_ips = dynamic(["178.236.252.133","77.91.123.187"]);
let c2_domains = dynamic(["hell1-kitty.cc","alphazero1-endscape.cc","api-microservice-us1.com","bucket-aws-s1.com","bucket-aws-s2.com","fileless-storage-s3.cc","globalsnn1-new.cc","globalsnn2-new.cc","globalsnn3-new.cc","handle-me-sv1.com","hardware-office.cc","health-smooth-eu1.com","health-smooth-eu2.com","health-smooth-eu3.com","holiday-updateservice.com","memory-protection-layer1.cc","memory-protection-layer2.cc","microservice-update-s1-bucket.cc","microservice-update-s2-bucket.cc","my-smart-house1.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
( ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstIpAddr in (c2_ips)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Dst=DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, Signal="NetworkToC2IP" ),
( ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (c2_domains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Dst=DnsQuery, DstPortNumber=int(null), Url="", Signal="DnsToC2Domain" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'

falsepositives:

      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high

let BadHashes = dynamic(["5f9ff671955a6d551595f9838aed063c496da5039be0d222fe84f96cb3e1d32a", "3c278499c5e3ced3bf1a6a7287808c5267075f1dec0aa5c7be2c4c444f33f2bc", "c68e436d4cb984db026210806f50d0c81eec5f6e4860197dab91fab6f31ef796", "e2faad8111e7d47349cbc549b85e62231b8678057906bc813aad7242fa95ae63", "e5e1d8ec4cd109df290752ee3d4b2cbc9de6df4360e9983548f1bc6b1d088540", "cbdfb46b9265a3dfb3bc6b0aade472dde28b1660dbd3ded3b67b1530b4497cca", "4a5e1d6ee1217e1fbacf54fc6017fbf9d24a25078266b02358d56a9c7437ceb7", "05becb67d8bf1e49fcfccb0d346b82368a2b1c2bf07316078c364c7b020154de", "44daa1b68737b55a711963eec211c7c018bcba4cb6d68c286a4b45ea781a7d73", "dc602cb53a9c24abfcdaadf0ca8256b5fb5cac6d91d20ed8431bdaaf51c0cafe", "10593dbe9edfde7943fdaadd7882f190216b2f6502667daf701088a6e810deaf", "0a69a9cc75d65774e5eb90a4a739bd4335d33b176dc4923acb691bd45af66bdf", "27c6a6bda2c0ef3ecb78dad9c6bb7c3abaf2e32b3ad96f372a0102c0c9c0f08d", "2cd449f1bb24f05d2e240812a74bd62f2583bbbe4d0ccc9ae5736240e29a0068", "30dcd5c71beb76d2f8df768d5fd9e9145cb8fbbfc951a63b969d26d3b64002b9", "dd4c7f5aae404816cf447b8090b620c1a1971a35c6791116aa3f871f00ae011b", "42a1fc74334c9a3b8720c79df55f84c7398bd31609eb10581e8c7155835498e3", "9c0d334aac5a6f66016dc5ce8df75c46d519a4e6d16c68cf2b1405c81189186d", "44f6313e9542c0d51937a70160fe4137012905d8c79ad27ccc0021788ecfaa4e"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GuardFall Exposes Open-Source AI Coding Agents to Decades-Old Shell Injection Risks

The Hacker News
2026-06-30 10 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

The safety check that is supposed to stop an AI coding agent from running a dangerous command can be walked straight past using a shell trick that has been public for decades. New research from&nbsp;Adversa AI, which is named the bypass GuardFall, found it works against ten of the eleven popular open-source coding and computer-use agents the firm tested. Only one, "Continue," was built to
